Notes: Ariile renale Left kidney is a little bit higher situated and also a little bit-1.5cm-longer than the right kidney. Kidney localisation: anatomical landmarks-last thoracic vertebrae till first lumbar vertebrae (D11-12 till L1-L2). Normal long axis around 10-14cm.

IV urography #5

  • unenhanced
  • 1-3(5) min
  • 15 min

Notes: 1: unenhanced 2: 1-3(5) min: nephrogram (visualization of the kidney ) 3: 15 min: visualization of renal pelvis, ureters, bladder

IV Urography: indications #6

  • Indications
  • -check for normal function of kidneys
  • -check for anatomical variants or congenital anomalies (e.g. -horse-shoe kidney)
  • -check the course of the ureters
  • -detect and localise a ureteric obstruction (urolithiasis)
  • -assess for synchronous upper tract disease in those with bladder transitional cell carcinoma (TCC)

IV urography 5 minutes: renal function #7

Notes: IVP gives information about kidney function too (secretion, excretion), not only morphology! Nephrogram (appears in seconds following i.v. injection of ultravist)= discrete opacity of renal parenchyma (contrast in kidney blood stream) Pyelogram = 🡪 contrast=white=opacity within the calyces, renal pelvis, urinary bladder 🡪 normally is synchronous, symmetrical and equal as intensity in both kidneys!!!!

Urography:The pelvicalyceal system #8

Diameter: 4-8 mm #9

  • Urography:Ureters
  • Segments:
  • Abdominal
  • Pelvic
  • Intramural

Notes: Normally you cannot see the entire ureter on an IVP image.You see segments of it. Why? Explanation: The urinary hydrostatic pressure in ureter is the same as in uriniferous tubules or Bowmann capsule=10mmHg. The urinary hydrostatic pressure in the bladder is 50mmHg. Thus, there are necessary peristaltic waves (ureter contraction) to push the urine from pyelon to bladder.

Notes: In the images above the ureters are visible almost on their entire length, because there is active compression on pelvis which determines contrast media reflux retrograde, into the ureters. Ectopia versus ptosis #22

  • Renal malformations

Notes: Usually an ectopic kidney will be also malrotated. Ectopia and malrotation predispose to infection, calculi and urinary stasis. First IVP: Ectopic and malrotated left kidney. The left kidney has from birth an abnormal, too low or ectopic position. Its ureter is shorter, not folded. Abnormal origin of kd vessells on arteriography-eg-illiac vessels. Second IVP: right kidney ptosis +malrotation + hydronephrosis. Left kidney ptosis with malrotation. The left kidney shows up on IVP under the illiac crest, the ureter has its normal length that is why it looks folded. Kidney ptosis occurs usually on elderly patients due to generalized hypotonia or in pt with previous significant abdominal surgery.Normal origin of renal vessels-hanging appearance on arteriography.

Ureteroceles #33

Notes: Ureterocoeles represent congenital dilatation of the distal-most portion of the ureter. The dilated portion of the ureter may herniate into the bladder secondary to the abnormal structure of vesicoureteric junction (VUJ). Epidemiology Most ureterocoeles are congenital, usually associated with ectopic insertion of the ureter with associated duplicated collecting system (see below).  In a minority of cases, ureteroceles are an isolated abnormality, and these are usually seen in adults

Litiaza renală #38

  • Pacientul care prezintă colică renală trebuie să fie examinat inițial cu ajutorul radiografiei renale simple pentru a identifica eventuali calculi radioopaci
  • 🡺 ariile de proiecție renale, uretere și vezica urinară
  • calculii pot fi - radioopaci = albi – vizibili pe RRS
  • - radiotransparenti = defecte de umplere pe urografie
  • Ulterior ecografie: calculi renali, hidronefroza, mai rar calculi ureterali (cu excepția ureterului terminal, lângă vezica urinara)
  • CT și uro-CT (controverse cu privire la radioprotectie)

  • Right hydronephrosis, both calyces and pelvis are dilated

  • Pyeloureteral junction syndrome

Notes: Se elimina dg de calcul. The cause of obstruction is usually a developmental defect of the muscle in this region. It can be due to other causes also, such as an abnormal renal artery in this region producing mechanical obstruction. Displazie fibromusculara sau vas polar inferior. UPJ Ureteropelvic junction (UPJ) obstruction is defined as an obstruction of the flow of urine from the renal pelvis to the proximal ureter. The condition is frequently encountered by both adult and pediatric urologists.
